chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Roped-off dances with White and Black sides
summary: Smith confirms big halls used a rope to separate White and Black dancers.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: One of the other guys, I think it was Buddy Tate, was telling me that at some of the dances, where you'd have some White and some Black, they'd put a rope down the middle.
Is that what they used to do?
Would that have been in just the small places?
We had one here, at the (?) Hall. When I played
out there, we had three bands there, and they had a rope right down the middle...
And you had White one side and Black the other.
And White on one side. And they broke that up.
